notes: Romano-British pottery, chemical composition by atomic absorption spectrophotometry for nine oxides, specimens grouped by kiln / find-site (Tubb, Parker & Nickless 1980, Archaeometry 22; HSAUR3 MANOVA / cluster example). Page lists nine oxide responses in page order Al2O3, Fe2O3, MgO, CaO, Na2O, K2O, TiO2, MnO, BaO and kiln as the site factor. Rule (a) multivariate split: model_index 1/2/3 = Al2O3/Fe2O3/MgO; the three-row cap leaves out CaO, Na2O, K2O, TiO2, MnO, BaO, filed in this row ignore. One-way kiln layout rendered as a kiln random intercept at low confidence; moved from the exclusions under rule (a). Hand sample #61: as pottery #3, HSAUR3 clusters the oxide measurements and fits no random-kiln regression. Retained kiln assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of kiln sites; this remains unverified.

Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 pottery: response Fe2O3 (iron trioxide). kiln random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al2O3); the other oxide responses in ignore. Hand sample #61: as pottery #3, HSAUR3 clusters the oxide measurements and fits no random-kiln regression. Retained kiln assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of kiln sites; this remains unverified.

Rule (a) multivariate split of HSAUR3 pottery: response MgO (magnesium oxide). kiln random intercept as in model_index 1 (Al2O3); the other oxide responses in ignore. Hand sample #61: HSAUR3 clusters the oxide measurements hierarchically and compares the clusters with the kilns; it fits no MgO random-kiln regression. Retained kiln assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of kiln sites; this remains unverified.

Inter-laboratory co-operative trial in analytical chemistry: seven specimens analysed by six laboratories in three batches each, every analysis duplicated (Analytical Methods Committee 1987; VR MASS 4th ed). Help page gives no model; rendered as a mixed model with a laboratory random effect, fixed specimen effects and batch nested within laboratory-specimen (the duplicates are the within-cell replication). Bat is nested within Spc/Lab per the help, so the batch term is the composite Lab:Spc:Bat built from its parts. Hand sample #61: MASS (scripts/ch10.R) documents Conc ~ 1 with random ~1|Lab/Bat restricted to Spc == "S1"; that fit does not establish the all-specimen model. Lab is fitted as random in that lme call (VR 4th ed, section 10.2). Spc is a design factor by the five-level rule: seven specimens (S1 to S7), the trial's test materials sent to every laboratory, which the S-PLUS code of VR section 10.2 declares not random (is.random(coop$Spc) <- F).

Barley field trial, 6 locations (Loc block) x 5 varieties; yields stored wide for 1931 (Y1) and 1932 (Y2); documented aov(cbind(Y1,Y2) ~ Loc + Var) and aov((Y1+Y2)/2 ~ Var + Loc), Loc the block. RULE GAP: the documented response is both year columns or their mean, not one column; filed Y1 with Y2 in ignore. Hand sample #12: the help models both year responses or their mean with Loc fixed, not Y1 alone with a random Loc. Retained Loc assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of locations; this remains unverified.

Classical NPK pea factorial on 6 blocks; documented aov(yield ~ block + N*P*K), block rendered as random (Census blocked-design rule). The fractional design confounds the N:P:K interaction with blocks; the reduced aov(yield ~ block + N + K) is a fixed-effects simplification (same model). The help example of stats::aov fits block as an Error() stratum, aov(yield ~ N*P*K + Error(block), npk), which is this row's model, marked "as a test, not particularly sensible statistically"; the proj and model.tables help pages repeat it.

Five sires, two dams within each sire, two progeny each; dam codes are reused within sire. The page says it appears to be a constructed data set, which is no statement of simulation, so it stays. Hand sample #11: Animal.Rd only calls str and the object's metadata gives AvgDailyGain ~ 1 | Sire/Dam; no inspected help or vignette fits the nested variance-components model. Regrouped by #45: the nested factor named as its composite, its codes repeating across its parent. Sire and Dam within Sire are fitted as random in the cited book, Littell et al. (1996), section 6.4 (Example: Obtaining BLUPs in a Random-Effects Model) on its Data Set 6.4, recalled from the book, whose text was not read.

formula: adg ~ line + damage + line:damage + weanage + weight + (1|sire)
notes: Help example fits a fixed-effects lm(adg ~ 1 + line + sire + damage + line:damage + weanage + weight) with sire fixed; Harvey 1960 (an early least-squares-means paper). RULE GAP: rendered as the classic sire variance-component model with sire (9 sires, nested in the 3 dam lines) as a random grouping factor; the dmm package vignette (cited) gives a full mixed analysis. calf is the steer row id (ignored); weanage and weight are continuous covariates. Harvey (1960, the model on p. 103 and Step 7 on p. 117) fits sires within lines as random and estimates their variance component, as the dmm vignette (dmmOverview.pdf, section 5.4) reports; this row's formula is that model.

Multi-environment potato trial (Tai 1971); yield is the mean of a 4-rep RCB at each environment, 48 genotype-environment cell means. variety is the genotype name (duplicate of gen); loc and year are the components of env; all ignored. Hand sample #11: the help gives a dotplot and a stability-analysis stub, not a crossed random-intercept model; Tai's stability analysis is not equivalent to it. env is fitted as random in Tai's stability analysis, which st4gi::tai (linked from the help) implements with fixed genotypes and random environments; this formula simplifies it by dropping each genotype's response to the environments, and Tai (1971) was not read (paywalled). gen is a design factor by the five-level rule: eight genotypes (G1 to G8), the trial's entries with Katahdin and Sebago as checks, fixed in Tai's analysis.

Multi-environment wheat trial (Vargas et al. 1998); help fits PLS of the GxE matrix on environmental covariates (sibling vargas.wheat2.covs). An environment random intercept with fixed genotype effects rendered from the 8-genotype by 21-environment design. RULE GAP: the stored yield is already environment- and genotype-centered (mean-zero GxE residuals, with negative values), so the main effects are near zero; the environment grouping is still real. Hand sample #12: the source fits PLS on the centred genotype-by-environment matrix, not crossed random intercepts. gen is a design factor by the five-level rule: eight genotypes (G1 to G8), the trial's entries, each a response column of the help's PLS fit.

formula: decision ~ rater + nation + language + location + (1 | judge)
notes: Fox 2016 (Applied Regression Analysis and GLMs 3e) uses the refugee-appeal data to study whether judges differ; the documented fit is a fixed-effects logistic, rendered here as a random-intercept logistic on judge per the Census fixed-blocked rule. judge is in the grouping list (10 judges, 384 cases). success is a derived nation-level logit of success rate, ignored. nation kept as a covariate (could alternatively be a crossed grouping). Retained judge assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of judges; this remains unverified.

8x8 Latin square of honeybee repellent (lime-sulphur) potency; rowpos and colpos are the Latin-square row and column blocks, treatment (A-H) the fixed factor; rendered with row and column random intercepts per the Census blocking rule. RULE GAP: the census coordinate rule (besag.checks) sends a field layout's row/col to ignore, but here rowpos/colpos are the design's blocking factors rather than mere spatial coordinates, so they are filed as grouping factors. Hand sample #12: published_model no stands; the Latin-square row and column blocks and the continuous decrease kept, no trials. Retained rowpos assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of row blocks; this remains unverified. Retained colpos assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of column blocks; this remains unverified.

Wedderburn (1974) quasi-binomial proportion example (also McCullagh & Nelder). 10 barley varieties at 9 sites, one obs per cell; blotch is a proportion with no trials column, filed continuous. Documented fit is fixed-effects on site and variety; rendered as random intercept on site (location block) per the Census blocking rule. Retained site assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of sites; this remains unverified.

Randomized complete block design (Anderson & Bancroft): 8 oat varieties in 5 blocks (heterogeneous growing area). Documented analysis is fixed-effects (yield ~ block + variety); rendered as random intercept on block per the Census blocking rule. Retained block assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of blocks; this remains unverified.

NIST Alaska-pipeline ultrasonic defect depths, field vs lab measurements taken in six batches (107 rows). Faraway fits a calibration regression Lab ~ Field ignoring batch; rendered with a random intercept on the named measurement Batch. RULE GAP: Batch is a data-collection batch, not a designed block. Retained Batch assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of measurement batches; this remains unverified.

RCBD: 5 varieties across 5 plots (replicate = plot as block). failure is failures out of 100 seeds (binomial, 100 trials, but no trials column so filed count). No model stated; rendered random per Census blocking rule, fixed fit failure ~ variety + replicate. Retained replicate assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of plots; this remains unverified.

Block = experimenter (blocking factor); Height, Frequency and resting heart rate fixed; Order is run order (ignored). No model stated; rendered random per Census blocking rule, fixed fit HR ~ Height*Frequency + RestHR. Retained Block assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of experimenter pairs; this remains unverified.

Faraway ELM binomial overdispersion example (fixed fit glm cbind(survive, total-survive) ~ location + period). location = stream block (5), period = retrieval time; rendered with location random per Census blocking rule. Retained location assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of stream locations; this remains unverified.

lattice help: Immer Minnesota barley multi-environment trial, 10 varieties x 6 sites x 2 years, yield averaged across 3 randomized blocks; help page gives only a dotplot example. site is the grouping; variety and year covariates. Block-averaged aggregate response on a real grouping, low per Census rule. Hand sample #12: published_model no stands; the documented example is a dotplot. Retained site assumes exchangeable sampling from a larger population of sites; this remains unverified.

Help page gives no model (only a stripplot of log(total.fruits+1)). RULE GAP: model rendered from Banta et al. 2010 / Bolker et al. 2009 design (clipping x nutrient fixed; population and genotype random; rack and germination status nuisance) with random intercepts only; reg ignored because popu is nested in it (popu codes carry the region). Bolker et al. (2009, Trends in Ecology and Evolution 24, Box 1) fit populations and genotypes within populations as random effects crossed with nutrient, clipping and their interaction; this formula simplifies that model to random intercepts.
